title: The div element and generic containers
learningObjectives: Explain the div element and generic containers and its role in modern HTML.
Select the correct elements, attributes, APIs, or browser behaviour for a practical use case.
Distinguish current practices from obsolete, limited, or legacy techniques.
Build and inspect a working example while considering accessibility and maintainability.
Diagnose common implementation errors and explain the trade-offs of the chosen approach.

understand.concept: The div element is a generic block container with no built-in semantic meaning. It is useful when a group needs a styling hook, layout wrapper, or script target and no more meaningful HTML element fits. A div should not replace header, nav, main, article, section, aside, footer, form, or button when one of those elements expresses the actual role. Class names should describe purpose or component identity rather than visual accidents. A div has no special keyboard interaction by default.
understand.whyItMatters: A page built from nested generic containers can be difficult to navigate and maintain. Choosing semantic elements first improves structure, accessibility, and code readability; div remains useful as a neutral grouping element.
understand.analogy: A div is an unlabeled box; it can group objects, but it does not tell someone what the group is for.
understand.analogyLimit: A generic box can still be useful in a semantic document; the goal is not to eliminate div, but to avoid using it when meaning exists.

explain.narrative: Compare a div-based page shell with a semantic page shell. Identify which wrappers are purely for layout and which regions have a recognized document role.

examples.explanation: The article carries meaning, while a class provides a styling hook. A div is unnecessary when a meaningful element fits.
examples.expectedOutput: A main region containing a lesson article.

examples.explanation: The div groups a layout collection; each card remains an article because each is independently meaningful.
examples.expectedOutput: A generic grid wrapper around two semantic articles.

practise.guidedTask: Inspect a page containing many div elements. Replace wrappers that represent navigation, main content, an article, or a footer with suitable semantic elements; keep div only for neutral grouping.
practise.independentTask: Create a component tree and explain the semantic purpose of every landmark. Test heading navigation and keyboard behaviour; do not add tabindex or ARIA roles to generic containers without a real interaction requirement.
hints: Choose elements by meaning, not by their default display style.
A div is not automatically focusable or interactive.
Use classes for reusable styling and IDs only when a unique identifier is required.

questions.prompt: What is the default semantic meaning of div?
options: It is a generic container with no special meaning
questions.answer: It is a generic container with no special meaning
questions.explanation: The div element groups content without adding a specific semantic role.

questions.prompt: When is a div a good choice?
options: When a neutral grouping or layout wrapper is needed
questions.answer: When a neutral grouping or layout wrapper is needed
questions.explanation: Use div when no more meaningful element fits the content or grouping.

questions.prompt: Which element should represent the primary page content?
questions.explanation: The main element identifies the document's primary content.

questions.prompt: Does a div become keyboard-interactive automatically?
options: Yes, every div is a button
Only when it has a class
questions.explanation: A div has no default interactive behaviour or keyboard focus.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest reason to prefer semantic HTML?
options: It communicates document roles to browsers, assistive technology, and developers
It guarantees every page is faster
It removes the need for CSS
questions.answer: It communicates document roles to browsers, assistive technology, and developers
questions.explanation: Semantic elements expose meaning and useful browser behaviour.
